title: Timing of a Damage Assessment and the Share Left Open to Challenge
content:
The timing of the damage assessment sets the share of the remaining amount left open to challenge on a
rental booked under the Car Rental Rate Classes. The days of the window used are the calendar days from the date the
renter returned the vehicle to the date the rental desk decided the last damage assessment it approved on
the rental, and they are measured against the damage reporting window published by the rate class booked.

**Where three times the days of the window used is more than twice the rate class's damage reporting
window**, 100 per cent is left open.

**Where three times the days of the window used is more than the rate class's damage reporting window**,
80 per cent is left open.

**Where three times the days of the window used is not more than the rate class's damage reporting window**,
neither of these shares applies to it.

## How the comparison is made

The comparison is made after trebling the days used, and the two rows are taken in the order they stand: a
rental meeting the first is answered by it and not by the second.

## Hypothetical illustration on a class whose damage reporting window is 10 calendar days

| Days of the window used | Three times that figure | More than twice the class's window, which is 20 | More than the class's window, which is 10 | Share left open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 6 | no | no | neither share applies |
| 3 | 9 | no | no | neither share applies |
| 4 | 12 | no | yes | 80 per cent |
| 6 | 18 | no | yes | 80 per cent |
| 7 | 21 | yes | yes | 100 per cent |

On a class whose window is 5 calendar days the same arithmetic runs against 10 and 5 instead, so 2 days used
gives 6, which is more than 5 but not more than 10, and 80 per cent is left open.
